Phrases that predict a talk

Which words and phrases are over-represented in talk abstracts compared with posters? Each phrase gets an odds ratio: how much more likely an abstract containing it is to be a talk.

Phrases are 1–3-word sequences from the abstract text. Variants of one idea that turn up in mostly the same abstracts (“massively parallel reporter”, “parallel reporter assay”, “MPRA”) are grouped under the best-scoring one, with the rest listed beneath it in small type.

15,327 abstracts, 1,544 of them talks: a pooled talk rate of 10.1%. Odds ratios are combined across years (Mantel–Haenszel, stratified by year), so a phrase that rose or fell over time isn't credited with each year's different baseline. 16 abstracts cut off in a booklet are left out of the phrase counts.

Phrase trends

Year by year, 2022–2026: the share of talks and of posters mentioning selected phrases.

Biobanks

How often abstracts mention the most-cited biobanks, 2022–2026, counting common acronyms (UKB, MVP, BBJ). UK Biobank is in about one abstract in eight every year; All of Us grew six-fold. To compare talks with posters for any of them, look it up below.

What changed in 2026

Clinical vocabulary stopped leaning toward posters. “Patients”, “likely pathogenic” and “next-generation sequencing” leaned toward posters over 2022–2025 (pooled odds ratios 0.4–0.7); in 2026 all three were at least as common in talks. Scanning every phrase for the largest 2026 shifts turns up more of the same: “idiopathic”, “genetic disease” and “therapy”.

Suggestive, not established. The top row was chosen before looking at 2026; the bottom row was picked for having the largest shifts, so its p-values overstate the evidence. Across all ~10,800 phrases tested, no single shift survives a false-discovery-rate correction.

Look up a phrase

The phrases above plus the top 50 each way across all years. See how often talks and posters mention a phrase each year, then which first-author institutions and metro areas write about it (among those with at least one talk mentioning it; an abstract counts for each of its institutions). Hover or focus a row for that institution's own mention rate. Searching also finds every other phrase in at least 5 talks over all years; for those the counts are exact matches in the abstract text (no titles or plurals), and there is no institution breakdown.
